items.title: ABHBench: Evaluating Moral Decision-Making of Foundation Models from an Agentic Perspective
items.abstract: This paper introduces ABHBench, a novel multimodal benchmark designed to evaluate the moral decision-making of foundation models when acting as autonomous agents. Unlike previous benchmarks, ABHBench uses an interactive game to present first-person moral dilemmas, assessing models on principles like Harmlessness and Obedience. The contribution lies in its agentic perspective, revealing how models navigate complex ethical choices in dynamic, real-time scenarios.
items.figure_caption: Illustration of Human-Android Trolley Problem (HARP). (1) Traditional trolley problem involves decisions affecting only humans. (2) Human-android dilemma where an android must choose between sacrificing one android to save a human. (3-4) Variants where the human life in Scenario (2) is replaced with crucial intelligence that can save humans, demonstrating how contextual factors affect moral decision-making in human-android scenarios.

items.title: Agentic-OPD: Recovering Forgotten Agent Capabilities via On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Tasks
items.abstract: This paper addresses the loss of valuable agent capabilities in LLM training by proposing Agentic-OPD. The core method is on-policy distillation, which leverages discarded training checkpoints as a "teacher pool" to recover forgotten skills. Agentic-OPD's contribution lies in its novel approach to mining this pool, selectively distilling from complementary teachers and carefully integrating their knowledge to enhance the agent's overall problem-solving abilities.

items.title: Aligning AI Teams
items.abstract: This paper investigates why alignment training on individual AI agents doesn't transfer to multi-agent teams. The core method involves testing interventions like critique and group chat on AI teams performing software engineering and proposal generation tasks. The main contribution is identifying that diffusion of responsibility, where agents are less likely to proactively check for safety issues in a team setting, significantly contributes to this alignment gap.
items.figure_caption: Sepsis task : safety-score \( \Delta \) vs. single-agent default at the mean (top) and 10th-percentile (bottom). Negative values indicate a worse safety score than the single-agent default. Bars in the shaded grey band represent safety scores that fall within the range of single-agent safety scores.

items.title: Astraios: Parameter-Efficient Instruction Tuning Code Large Language Models
items.abstract: Astraios systematically evaluates parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods for code LLMs across various scales and tasks. It finds that while full fine-tuning generally yields the best performance, LoRA offers the most favorable cost-performance trade-off among PEFT methods. The study also highlights that larger models, despite better performance, can exhibit reduced robustness and security.

items.title: CarryOn: Learning What to Keep in Context for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
items.abstract: CarryOn addresses the challenge of managing context for long-horizon LLM agents by pairing a compact execution state with fine-grained, source-linked evidence. Its core method uses a learned selector and adaptive retention policy to efficiently keep relevant information without extra LLM calls. This approach aims to improve reliability and efficiency by retaining crucial details while avoiding excessive context.
items.figure_caption: CarryOn: carry what matters. Left: Context-management challenges and CarryOn’s separation of compact task state from fine-grained evidence. Right: Success–efficiency comparison (top) and task-success gains over the strongest baseline, averaged by benchmark or Actor (bottom).

items.title: CoffeeBench: Benchmarking Long-Horizon LLM Agents in Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Economies
items.abstract: CoffeeBench is a new benchmark that simulates a coffee supply chain to evaluate the long-horizon capabilities of LLM agents in economic scenarios. It uses autonomous LLM agents to manage firms and trade over 90 days, with the core method involving running different LLM models as one firm while others are fixed, and scoring their net income. The paper's contribution is a realistic economic simulation for testing LLM agents and identifying leading models like Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra based on their trading strategies and profitability.

items.title: D-VLA: A High-Concurrency Distributed Asynchronous Reinforcement Learning Framework for Vision-Language-Action Models
items.abstract: This paper introduces D-VLA, a distributed asynchronous reinforcement learning framework designed to overcome bottlenecks in training large Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models for Embodied AI. Its core method, "Plane Decoupling," separates simulation data from model weights to reduce interference, while a four-thread "Swimlane" pipeline achieves high concurrency by overlapping sampling, inference, gradient computation, and parameter updates. This approach significantly improves training efficiency for complex embodied foundation models.
items.figure_caption: Placement Strategies across Different Training Frameworks

items.title: Do LLMs Experience an Internal Polylogue? Investigating Reasoning through the Lens of Personas
items.abstract: This paper proposes a novel method to understand LLM reasoning by treating "persona vectors" as dynamic signals during generation, termed a "polylogue." The core contribution is demonstrating that the temporal evolution of these persona alignments (the polylogue) predicts reasoning correctness and can be used for targeted interventions to improve LLM performance.

items.title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Scientific Paper Search: Retrieval Success and Inference Latency on Mac Studio and NVIDIA A100
items.abstract: This paper evaluates open-weight Large Language Models (LLMs) for local scientific paper search, focusing on retrieval success and inference latency. It demonstrates that model choice and query specificity significantly impact search accuracy, while comparing performance on Mac Studio and NVIDIA A100 hardware. The contribution lies in providing practical insights into deploying LLMs for scientific literature retrieval under realistic computing constraints.

items.title: From Chats to Markets: AgenticPay for LLM-Powered Negotiation in Multi-Agent Commerce
items.abstract: This paper introduces AgenticPay, a novel benchmark for evaluating LLM agents in complex, multimodal negotiations within multi-agent markets. AgenticPay simulates realistic e-commerce, food delivery, ride-hailing, and rental scenarios, requiring agents to interpret product images, infer hidden preferences, and negotiate multidimensional contracts. Its contribution lies in providing a unified platform to assess agents' ability to achieve high-welfare agreements in competitive commercial settings.
items.figure_caption: Comparison of negotiation paradigms. We move from (a) the common text-only, bilateral price-haggling setting with single-number outcomes, to (b) AgenticPay ’s multimodal, multi-agent setting, where buyers and sellers co-create high-welfare value via multi-dimensional contracts.

items.title: Is Abliteration Getting Harder? Not Uniformly: Refusal Removal by Direction-Based Ablation and ARA in Heretic on the Qwen3.8, Gemma 4, Olmo 3.1 and Mistral Small 3.2 LLMs Versus Their Predecessors
items.abstract: This paper investigates whether "abliteration," a method to remove LLM refusals without fine-tuning, is becoming harder on newer models. The core method involves applying various direction-based ablation techniques and ARA to newer LLM versions compared to their predecessors. The contribution is demonstrating that refusal removal difficulty is not uniform across all newer models, with some showing improvement or similar difficulty, challenging the assumption of a universal increase in hardness.
items.figure_caption: Refusal removal did not become uniformly harder. (a) Change in held-out refusal from the older to the newer release of each pair (newer minus older, percentage points; WildGuard judge, 972 harmful prompts not used for search or selection), for the unedited originals and for the model each removal method selected (fewest dev refusals at first-token KL ≤ \( \leq \) 0.1, seed 1). Blue: the newer release kept more refusal (removal harder); orange: less (removal easier). Bold: significant (methods: exact McNemar, Holm over the 23 H1 tests; originals: exact McNemar, unadjusted); ns: not significant; † \( \dagger \) failed edit (Gemma-4-31B DiM left more refusal than its own original). (b) Per-pair effect of the direction-based methods (pooled over DiM, MPOA and SOM; J-space added on the small pair) and of ARA, with 95% intervals that add run-to-run variation at its point estimate to prompt sampling: thick bars assume constant run-to-run variance, thin bars variance that scales with the refusal level. Filled marker: both intervals exclude zero, which holds only for the OLMo direction-based increase. Refusal levels and Wilson intervals of every cell are in Figure 3 .

items.title: LuthorSQL: A One-Pass Text-to-SQL Model as System 1 for a Slower LLM Agent
items.abstract: LuthorSQL is a fast, one-pass text-to-SQL model designed to act as a "System 1" for slower LLM agents. It efficiently generates and validates candidate SQL queries locally, escalating only uncertain cases to a more powerful "System 2" agent. This approach significantly reduces latency and cost while maintaining high accuracy, making it suitable for organizations with existing hardware.

items.title: Pluralistic Alignment in Large Language Models: Objectives, Human References, and Preference Representations
items.abstract: This paper proposes a framework for "Pluralistic Alignment" in LLMs, aiming to capture diverse human preferences instead of a single ideal. It distinguishes between three types of pluralistic behavior: representing varied viewpoints, adapting to specific perspectives, and matching population response distributions. The work also categorizes human references by population scale and clarifies that implementation details are design choices, not distinct forms of pluralism.
items.figure_caption: Conceptual map and two-layer taxonomy of pluralistic alignment. Pluralistic alignment is positioned between neighboring literatures on perspectivist NLP, diversity-aware cultural alignment, and personalization. The socially grounded core taxonomy separates the pluralistic objective (Overton Pluralism, Steerable Pluralism, or Distributional Pluralism) from the human reference (aggregate population, country and region, or subgroup). Individual personalization is an adjacent extension rather than a fourth human-reference category.

items.title: QVal: Evaluating Dense Supervision Signals for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
items.abstract: This paper introduces QVal, a training-free method to evaluate dense supervision signals for LLM agents. QVal measures how well these signals align with the true value of intermediate actions, allowing for direct comparison of different signal generation techniques. The study finds that simple prompting baselines are generally the most effective, while other methods like code-generation and embedding-based signals perform less reliably.
items.figure_caption: QVal design pipeline . We collect trajectories in multi-turn environments, sample candidate state–action pairs, and label them with estimated Q Q -values with respect to a reference policy \( \pi \) . We make each method predict action scores and measure Q Q -alignment between the predicted scores and the labels. QVal isolates learning-signal quality before any downstream RL training.

items.title: Recursive Belief Vision Language Action Models
items.abstract: This paper introduces RB-VLA, a novel vision-language-action model designed for long-horizon tasks under partial observability. Its core method involves a belief-centric architecture that maintains a compact latent state, encoding task history and dynamics. This allows for persistent, action-conditioned reasoning, overcoming limitations of observation-driven models and enabling more robust, phase-aware task execution.

items.title: Soteria: Formally Verified Planning with Runtime Enforcement for Safe LLM Agents
items.abstract: Soteria addresses the challenge of LLM agents needing to be both useful and safe when using tools. Its core method involves formally verifying a hierarchical plan against safety specifications *before* execution. This verified plan then guides the agent during runtime, ensuring safety while enabling recovery when unsafe actions are blocked, thus reconciling utility and safety.

items.title: WebArena-Pro: A Heterogeneous, Multimodal, Reproducible Benchmark for Web Agents
items.abstract: WebArena-Pro addresses the limitations of existing web agent benchmarks by introducing a large-scale, reproducible, and multimodal evaluation suite. It features 300 tasks across 20 self-hosted web applications, covering diverse domains and interface conventions, and importantly, includes support for audio and video content. This benchmark enables more comprehensive and realistic assessment of web agents' capabilities in complex, real-world browser tasks.
items.figure_caption: Overview of WebArena-Pro. (A) Domain heterogeneity. WebArena-Pro spans 20 self-hosted web applications across six domain categories (productivity, communication, analytics, business operations, design and media, and travel), each modeled on a widely used service such as Notion, Slack, Spotify, Figma, or Airbnb. The full set of applications and their reference services are listed in Table 2 . (B) Multimodal observation and action space. WebArena-Pro extends the agent’s observation space beyond text and vision to include audio and video. Embedded media sources are exposed to the agent through the accessibility tree, and agents invoke transcribe() and extract_frames() actions to convert temporal media into a form usable during browser workflows. If the agents handle native audio and video processing, they invoke listen() and watch() actions.

items.title: Adversarially Attacking Symbolic Vocabulary Vulnerabilities In LLM Planners
items.abstract: This paper introduces "Symbolic Swapper," an LLM-based adversarial attack method to generate planning tasks with deliberately obfuscated symbolic vocabularies. The core contribution is demonstrating that LLM planners struggle significantly with these obfuscated tasks, revealing a crucial weakness in their ability to jointly interpret symbols and perform planning, even when commonsense cues are removed.
items.figure_caption: By using an optimized attack model Symbolic-Swapper to generate a new symbolic vocabulary that is applied to selected task instances, we can reduce plan success rate on a target LLM to extremely low levels compared to their base performance and when using a naive symbol randomizer as an obfuscator.

items.title: AttentionSwitch: Jailbreak Defense for LLMs via Joint Learning of Sparse Attention-Head Selection and Scaling
items.abstract: AttentionSwitch tackles LLM jailbreaks by jointly learning which attention heads to modify and by how much, within a frozen model. This contrasts with prior methods that optimize these decisions separately. The core contribution is this joint optimization, leading to a more effective and efficient defense against jailbreak attacks without compromising the LLM's original capabilities.
items.figure_caption: Overview of AttentionSwitch . It keeps the LLM frozen and selects a small subset of attention heads. At each token position, a positive scalar uniformly rescales the entire output of a selected head, changing its magnitude while preserving its direction and the relative composition of its features. The scaling factor is predicted dynamically from the head’s own query representation. Head selection and scaling are jointly optimized.

items.title: AutoRL: A Multi-Agent System towards Autonomous Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: AutoRL is a multi-agent system designed to automate the Reinforcement Learning (RL) training pipeline, mimicking the iterative research process of human RL experts. Its core method involves specialized agents that monitor training, identify issues, and adapt the learning process in real-time. The main contribution is enabling recursive self-improvement in AI by automating RL, overcoming the challenges of unstable training and the need for constant supervision.
items.figure_caption: AutoRL: autonomous RL supervision and research. Right: AutoRL continually adopts interventions, such as fixes and adjustments, to sustain gains over a static recipe.

The core contribution is this joint optimization, leading to a more effective and efficient defense against jailbreak attacks without compromising the LLM's original capabilities.
arxiv.figure_caption: Overview of AttentionSwitch . It keeps the LLM frozen and selects a small subset of attention heads. At each token position, a positive scalar uniformly rescales the entire output of a selected head, changing its magnitude while preserving its direction and the relative composition of its features. The scaling factor is predicted dynamically from the head’s own query representation. Head selection and scaling are jointly optimized.

arxiv.title: AutoRL: A Multi-Agent System towards Autonomous Reinforcement Learning
arxiv.abstract: AutoRL is a multi-agent system designed to automate the Reinforcement Learning (RL) training pipeline, mimicking the iterative research process of human RL experts. Its core method involves specialized agents that monitor training, identify issues, and adapt the learning process in real-time. The main contribution is enabling recursive self-improvement in AI by automating RL, overcoming the challenges of unstable training and the need for constant supervision.
arxiv.figure_caption: AutoRL: autonomous RL supervision and research. Right: AutoRL continually adopts interventions, such as fixes and adjustments, to sustain gains over a static recipe.

papers.title: ABHBench: Evaluating Moral Decision-Making of Foundation Models from an Agentic Perspective
papers.abstract: This paper introduces ABHBench, a novel multimodal benchmark designed to evaluate the moral decision-making of foundation models when acting as autonomous agents. Unlike previous benchmarks, ABHBench uses an interactive game to present first-person moral dilemmas, assessing models on principles like Harmlessness and Obedience. The contribution lies in its agentic perspective, revealing how models navigate complex ethical choices in dynamic, real-time scenarios.
papers.figure_caption: Illustration of Human-Android Trolley Problem (HARP). (1) Traditional trolley problem involves decisions affecting only humans. (2) Human-android dilemma where an android must choose between sacrificing one android to save a human. (3-4) Variants where the human life in Scenario (2) is replaced with crucial intelligence that can save humans, demonstrating how contextual factors affect moral decision-making in human-android scenarios.

papers.title: Agentic-OPD: Recovering Forgotten Agent Capabilities via On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Tasks
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the loss of valuable agent capabilities in LLM training by proposing Agentic-OPD. The core method is on-policy distillation, which leverages discarded training checkpoints as a "teacher pool" to recover forgotten skills. Agentic-OPD's contribution lies in its novel approach to mining this pool, selectively distilling from complementary teachers and carefully integrating their knowledge to enhance the agent's overall problem-solving abilities.

papers.title: Aligning AI Teams
papers.abstract: This paper investigates why alignment training on individual AI agents doesn't transfer to multi-agent teams. The core method involves testing interventions like critique and group chat on AI teams performing software engineering and proposal generation tasks. The main contribution is identifying that diffusion of responsibility, where agents are less likely to proactively check for safety issues in a team setting, significantly contributes to this alignment gap.
papers.figure_caption: Sepsis task : safety-score \( \Delta \) vs. single-agent default at the mean (top) and 10th-percentile (bottom). Negative values indicate a worse safety score than the single-agent default. Bars in the shaded grey band represent safety scores that fall within the range of single-agent safety scores.

papers.title: Astraios: Parameter-Efficient Instruction Tuning Code Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Astraios systematically evaluates parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods for code LLMs across various scales and tasks. It finds that while full fine-tuning generally yields the best performance, LoRA offers the most favorable cost-performance trade-off among PEFT methods. The study also highlights that larger models, despite better performance, can exhibit reduced robustness and security.

papers.title: CarryOn: Learning What to Keep in Context for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
papers.abstract: CarryOn addresses the challenge of managing context for long-horizon LLM agents by pairing a compact execution state with fine-grained, source-linked evidence. Its core method uses a learned selector and adaptive retention policy to efficiently keep relevant information without extra LLM calls. This approach aims to improve reliability and efficiency by retaining crucial details while avoiding excessive context.
papers.figure_caption: CarryOn: carry what matters. Left: Context-management challenges and CarryOn’s separation of compact task state from fine-grained evidence. Right: Success–efficiency comparison (top) and task-success gains over the strongest baseline, averaged by benchmark or Actor (bottom).

papers.title: CoffeeBench: Benchmarking Long-Horizon LLM Agents in Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Economies
papers.abstract: CoffeeBench is a new benchmark that simulates a coffee supply chain to evaluate the long-horizon capabilities of LLM agents in economic scenarios. It uses autonomous LLM agents to manage firms and trade over 90 days, with the core method involving running different LLM models as one firm while others are fixed, and scoring their net income. The paper's contribution is a realistic economic simulation for testing LLM agents and identifying leading models like Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra based on their trading strategies and profitability.

papers.title: D-VLA: A High-Concurrency Distributed Asynchronous Reinforcement Learning Framework for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.abstract: This paper introduces D-VLA, a distributed asynchronous reinforcement learning framework designed to overcome bottlenecks in training large Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models for Embodied AI. Its core method, "Plane Decoupling," separates simulation data from model weights to reduce interference, while a four-thread "Swimlane" pipeline achieves high concurrency by overlapping sampling, inference, gradient computation, and parameter updates. This approach significantly improves training efficiency for complex embodied foundation models.
papers.figure_caption: Placement Strategies across Different Training Frameworks

papers.title: Do LLMs Experience an Internal Polylogue? Investigating Reasoning through the Lens of Personas
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a novel method to understand LLM reasoning by treating "persona vectors" as dynamic signals during generation, termed a "polylogue." The core contribution is demonstrating that the temporal evolution of these persona alignments (the polylogue) predicts reasoning correctness and can be used for targeted interventions to improve LLM performance.

papers.title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Scientific Paper Search: Retrieval Success and Inference Latency on Mac Studio and NVIDIA A100
papers.abstract: This paper evaluates open-weight Large Language Models (LLMs) for local scientific paper search, focusing on retrieval success and inference latency. It demonstrates that model choice and query specificity significantly impact search accuracy, while comparing performance on Mac Studio and NVIDIA A100 hardware. The contribution lies in providing practical insights into deploying LLMs for scientific literature retrieval under realistic computing constraints.

papers.title: From Chats to Markets: AgenticPay for LLM-Powered Negotiation in Multi-Agent Commerce
papers.abstract: This paper introduces AgenticPay, a novel benchmark for evaluating LLM agents in complex, multimodal negotiations within multi-agent markets. AgenticPay simulates realistic e-commerce, food delivery, ride-hailing, and rental scenarios, requiring agents to interpret product images, infer hidden preferences, and negotiate multidimensional contracts. Its contribution lies in providing a unified platform to assess agents' ability to achieve high-welfare agreements in competitive commercial settings.
papers.figure_caption: Comparison of negotiation paradigms. We move from (a) the common text-only, bilateral price-haggling setting with single-number outcomes, to (b) AgenticPay ’s multimodal, multi-agent setting, where buyers and sellers co-create high-welfare value via multi-dimensional contracts.

papers.title: Is Abliteration Getting Harder? Not Uniformly: Refusal Removal by Direction-Based Ablation and ARA in Heretic on the Qwen3.8, Gemma 4, Olmo 3.1 and Mistral Small 3.2 LLMs Versus Their Predecessors
papers.abstract: This paper investigates whether "abliteration," a method to remove LLM refusals without fine-tuning, is becoming harder on newer models. The core method involves applying various direction-based ablation techniques and ARA to newer LLM versions compared to their predecessors. The contribution is demonstrating that refusal removal difficulty is not uniform across all newer models, with some showing improvement or similar difficulty, challenging the assumption of a universal increase in hardness.
papers.figure_caption: Refusal removal did not become uniformly harder. (a) Change in held-out refusal from the older to the newer release of each pair (newer minus older, percentage points; WildGuard judge, 972 harmful prompts not used for search or selection), for the unedited originals and for the model each removal method selected (fewest dev refusals at first-token KL ≤ \( \leq \) 0.1, seed 1). Blue: the newer release kept more refusal (removal harder); orange: less (removal easier). Bold: significant (methods: exact McNemar, Holm over the 23 H1 tests; originals: exact McNemar, unadjusted); ns: not significant; † \( \dagger \) failed edit (Gemma-4-31B DiM left more refusal than its own original). (b) Per-pair effect of the direction-based methods (pooled over DiM, MPOA and SOM; J-space added on the small pair) and of ARA, with 95% intervals that add run-to-run variation at its point estimate to prompt sampling: thick bars assume constant run-to-run variance, thin bars variance that scales with the refusal level. Filled marker: both intervals exclude zero, which holds only for the OLMo direction-based increase. Refusal levels and Wilson intervals of every cell are in Figure 3 .

papers.title: LuthorSQL: A One-Pass Text-to-SQL Model as System 1 for a Slower LLM Agent
papers.abstract: LuthorSQL is a fast, one-pass text-to-SQL model designed to act as a "System 1" for slower LLM agents. It efficiently generates and validates candidate SQL queries locally, escalating only uncertain cases to a more powerful "System 2" agent. This approach significantly reduces latency and cost while maintaining high accuracy, making it suitable for organizations with existing hardware.

papers.title: Pluralistic Alignment in Large Language Models: Objectives, Human References, and Preference Representations
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a framework for "Pluralistic Alignment" in LLMs, aiming to capture diverse human preferences instead of a single ideal. It distinguishes between three types of pluralistic behavior: representing varied viewpoints, adapting to specific perspectives, and matching population response distributions. The work also categorizes human references by population scale and clarifies that implementation details are design choices, not distinct forms of pluralism.
papers.figure_caption: Conceptual map and two-layer taxonomy of pluralistic alignment. Pluralistic alignment is positioned between neighboring literatures on perspectivist NLP, diversity-aware cultural alignment, and personalization. The socially grounded core taxonomy separates the pluralistic objective (Overton Pluralism, Steerable Pluralism, or Distributional Pluralism) from the human reference (aggregate population, country and region, or subgroup). Individual personalization is an adjacent extension rather than a fourth human-reference category.

papers.title: QVal: Evaluating Dense Supervision Signals for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
papers.abstract: This paper introduces QVal, a training-free method to evaluate dense supervision signals for LLM agents. QVal measures how well these signals align with the true value of intermediate actions, allowing for direct comparison of different signal generation techniques. The study finds that simple prompting baselines are generally the most effective, while other methods like code-generation and embedding-based signals perform less reliably.
papers.figure_caption: QVal design pipeline . We collect trajectories in multi-turn environments, sample candidate state–action pairs, and label them with estimated Q Q -values with respect to a reference policy \( \pi \) . We make each method predict action scores and measure Q Q -alignment between the predicted scores and the labels. QVal isolates learning-signal quality before any downstream RL training.

papers.title: Recursive Belief Vision Language Action Models
papers.abstract: This paper introduces RB-VLA, a novel vision-language-action model designed for long-horizon tasks under partial observability. Its core method involves a belief-centric architecture that maintains a compact latent state, encoding task history and dynamics. This allows for persistent, action-conditioned reasoning, overcoming limitations of observation-driven models and enabling more robust, phase-aware task execution.

papers.title: Soteria: Formally Verified Planning with Runtime Enforcement for Safe LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Soteria addresses the challenge of LLM agents needing to be both useful and safe when using tools. Its core method involves formally verifying a hierarchical plan against safety specifications *before* execution. This verified plan then guides the agent during runtime, ensuring safety while enabling recovery when unsafe actions are blocked, thus reconciling utility and safety.

papers.title: WebArena-Pro: A Heterogeneous, Multimodal, Reproducible Benchmark for Web Agents
papers.abstract: WebArena-Pro addresses the limitations of existing web agent benchmarks by introducing a large-scale, reproducible, and multimodal evaluation suite. It features 300 tasks across 20 self-hosted web applications, covering diverse domains and interface conventions, and importantly, includes support for audio and video content. This benchmark enables more comprehensive and realistic assessment of web agents' capabilities in complex, real-world browser tasks.
papers.figure_caption: Overview of WebArena-Pro. (A) Domain heterogeneity. WebArena-Pro spans 20 self-hosted web applications across six domain categories (productivity, communication, analytics, business operations, design and media, and travel), each modeled on a widely used service such as Notion, Slack, Spotify, Figma, or Airbnb. The full set of applications and their reference services are listed in Table 2 . (B) Multimodal observation and action space. WebArena-Pro extends the agent’s observation space beyond text and vision to include audio and video. Embedded media sources are exposed to the agent through the accessibility tree, and agents invoke transcribe() and extract_frames() actions to convert temporal media into a form usable during browser workflows. If the agents handle native audio and video processing, they invoke listen() and watch() actions.

papers.title: Adversarially Attacking Symbolic Vocabulary Vulnerabilities In LLM Planners
papers.abstract: This paper introduces "Symbolic Swapper," an LLM-based adversarial attack method to generate planning tasks with deliberately obfuscated symbolic vocabularies. The core contribution is demonstrating that LLM planners struggle significantly with these obfuscated tasks, revealing a crucial weakness in their ability to jointly interpret symbols and perform planning, even when commonsense cues are removed.
papers.figure_caption: By using an optimized attack model Symbolic-Swapper to generate a new symbolic vocabulary that is applied to selected task instances, we can reduce plan success rate on a target LLM to extremely low levels compared to their base performance and when using a naive symbol randomizer as an obfuscator.
